subject.title: feat: Tiered bootstrap file loading for progressive context control

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and what defaults and hook-extra semantics should the linked implementation use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a new config/default surface changes prompt context, session behavior, hook extras, and upgrade expectations in a way automation should not decide.

options.title: Sponsor the linked PR shape
options.body: Proceed with maintainer review of the linked PR as the focused additive config path, requiring unchanged no-override defaults plus docs/tests for resolver, hook, schema, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap selection
options.body: Pause this issue behind https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46565 and design one public selector contract that covers tiering, session filtering, and prompt-pressure work together.

options.title: Decline a new config knob
options.body: Keep the current fixed filters and steer users toward existing contextInjection, budget, lightweight, or doctor guidance instead of adding `bootstrapTier`.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the linked PR shape
recommendation.body: Proceed with maintainer review of the linked PR as the focused additive config path, requiring unchanged no-override defaults plus docs/tests for resolver, hook, schema, and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history and prior review signal for the bootstrap filtering and config-surface decision.
